name_note: The GTDB genus Micrococcus corresponds to the classical genus of that name; most of its genomes are Micrococcus luteus, the species these sentences describe.

sentences.text: Micrococcus luteus is a gram-positive, coagulase-negative coccus commonly regarded as a non-pathogenic commensal organism of human skin.
A comparative genomic study calls it ubiquitously distributed, selecting strains from six different isolation sources, with genome sizes ranging from 2.4 to 2.8 Mb.
It is a high-GC gram-positive species that has been recognized historically for natural transformation, the uptake of extracellular DNA into the genome.
A study reported that a skin isolate of M. luteus attenuated Staphylococcus aureus-induced release of IL-33 and TSLP from keratinocytes through a secreted serine protease.
Although frequently considered a contaminant in blood cultures, it has been reported as an opportunistic pathogen, including a case of septic shock with repeatedly positive cultures.
